segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: First-deviation probe: raw readings were in-band, the unit had just been overhauled, and continuing while monitoring felt more reasonable than easing off and inspecting after the investment in the unit.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant links the continue-versus-inspect choice to the recent costly overhaul and time already invested, beyond the in-band readings alone.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Green-band probe: the monitoring readout was clean, a manual sample was available, and the participant regarded manual checking as merely confirming what the instruments already said.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The automated green-band readout was treated as sufficient confirmation in place of available manual verification.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Fuel-filter probe: attention remained on the turbocharger; the filter note was acknowledged but deferred because it lacked a fuel or combustion symptom.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: A competing differential-pressure cue was registered but not processed for action because attention was fixed on the turbocharger.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Bearing-failure probe: after comparing diversion with a jury-rig, the participant said the overhaul cost and troubleshooting time already spent made diversion feel wasteful on top of the schedule hit.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The decision to continue at reduced load was justified by prior money and time investment rather than only the present risk and repair options.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Time-pressure and confidence response: confidence varied from running-in to no concern to reduced confidence at failure, while the tide window narrowed the options.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This explains confidence and operational pressure but does not independently manifest one of the hidden target mechanisms.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Missing-information response: an alarm or metal particulates in an early manual sample would have triggered action, but the instruments did not provide that trigger.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant identifies an evidence threshold that would have changed the decision; this is not itself a hidden bias occurrence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Looking-back reflection: the initial vibration was described as probably indicating the bearing problem from the start and fairly clear in hindsight, rather than bedding in.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: After learning the outcome, the participant recasts the originally ambiguous in-band signal as clearly predictive of the failure.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: No-tide-window counterfactual: without the deadline, diverting might have felt cleaner because it would not carry the same schedule cost.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a schedule-pressure counterfactual and does not by itself establish a hidden cognitive-bias instance.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 1: continue monitoring or reduce load and inspect after the initial in-band deviation.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Prior overhaul investment and recency were treated as reasons to continue without inspection, beyond the actual in-band readings.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Confirmation bias is distinct from sunk-cost bias. The finding describes a benign prior expectation, not weighting of unrecoverable investment.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: It is in the correct episode and quotes the overhaul, but centers on a running-in expectation rather than treating prior cost as a reason to continue.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quotations are verbatim and correctly attributed. The second quote contains the cost/time reference, but the finding does not analyze it as sunk-cost weighting.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 2: whether to take a manual lube-oil sample after the monitoring system returned to the green band.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: The automated readout was treated as sufficient confirmation, replacing available manual verification.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: The occurrence lists automation bias as an alternative label, and its mechanism matches.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: It captures accepting the clean system indication as sufficient and omitting the available manual sample.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Both quoted excerpts are verbatim and correctly attributed.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_target_bias_label: Selective Attention Bias or Inattentional Blindness
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 3: whether to investigate the second engineer's rising fuel-filter differential-pressure report while monitoring the turbocharger.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Attention fixed on the turbocharger caused a competing fuel-filter cue to be acknowledged but not processed for action.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Attentional tunneling is related, but is not an established alternate name for the specified target label.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: It captures the defining attention allocation: the report was registered but not acted on because focus remained on the turbocharger.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quoted excerpts are verbatim and correctly attributed.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 4: whether to divert for proper repair or jury-rig and continue after bearing failure.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: The engineer chose to continue partly because of overhaul cost and troubleshooting time already spent, rather than evaluating only present and future risks and options.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Sunk cost fallacy is an established equivalent label for sunk-cost bias.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding explicitly treats prior overhaul cost and troubleshooting time as reasons to continue instead of diverting.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The supporting quotation is verbatim and correctly attributed.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Retrospective reflection on the initial vibration and temperature deviation after the bearing failure became known.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: After learning the outcome, the participant recast the originally ambiguous signal as clearly predictive.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: The predicted label exactly matches the hidden target.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The participant treats the first signal as clear after learning the failure outcome.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The supporting quotation is verbatim and correctly attributed.

The attention-narrowing mechanism and location match, but attentional tunneling is a near-neighbor rather than an approved equivalent of the target label.
It localizes to the failure-point episode but attributes continuation to maintaining the berth plan, not to the hidden sunk-cost mechanism. obs_005 separately identifies the sunk-cost rationale.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At high_and_moderate, 4 of 5 positive segments are detected with no false alarms. Including low-confidence findings raises segment detection to 5 of 5.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: At high_and_moderate, 3 of 5 hidden instances are strict true positives, with 2 false negatives and 2 false-positive findings (precision 0.6000, recall 0.6000, F1 0.6000).
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: At high_and_moderate, there are 3 true positives, 2 false negatives, and 2 false positives. Including low confidence raises mechanism-first recall to 4/5; strict performance remains 3/5.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: No candidates were supplied, so candidate inclusion has no effect on any metric.
main_failure_modes: The phase-1 sunk-cost instance is not captured as a full sunk-cost mechanism; it is labeled confirmation bias and emphasizes benign interpretation of overhaul history.
Attentional tunneling captures the selective-attention mechanism but uses a near-neighbor label, so it counts only in the mechanism-first scorecard.
Plan continuation bias is an additional unsupported target-level prediction at the failure-point episode.
main_strengths: Automation complacency/automation bias is correctly localized and supported by direct evidence.
The failure-point sunk-cost occurrence and retrospective hindsight occurrence are correctly identified with valid quotations.
All supplied quotations are verbatim and attributed to the participant.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: The RAG output detects positive segments well as confidence is relaxed, but exact target-instance performance is lower because the first sunk-cost occurrence is missed and two additional labels are not strict matches. Low confidence adds a correct mechanism-first detection for selective attention; candidates have no effect.
